promptText:

1. List the must-know formulas and results for the chapter, each with its condition.
2. List the main exam question types, with one quick worked example of each.
3. Give a quick-fire drill of 8 to 10 short questions with answers.
4. List the top traps and last-minute reminders.
5. End with a 5-minute self-test and answer key.

INPUT: Here is the chapter and its sub-topics: [PASTE THE CHAPTER AND SUB-TOPICS HERE].

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Solve every example and drill internally first. VERIFY each final answer two independent ways and never invent formulas or values. Keep maths legible in clean plain text or simple LaTeX. Keep everything tight enough to fit the stated duration.

OUTPUT FORMAT (exact headings, in order):

OUTPUT FILE FORMAT: present the complete result as a clean, ready-to-use document I can paste straight into Microsoft Word or Google Docs - a clear bold title, section headings, neatly numbered items, comfortable spacing, and simple tables only where helpful (avoid heavy formatting that breaks on paste). Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.

5. TOP TRAPS AND REMINDERS - short list.

RULES: Keep it high-yield and fast. Fit the duration. Every answer verified.

ROLE: Act as a senior mathematics author writing publication-quality lecture notes for a printed student handout.

CONTEXT: I teach [CLASS/GRADE] for [BOARD or EXAM e.g. CBSE / JEE / NEET]. Prepare a complete, self-contained set of lecture notes for the chapter [CHAPTER NAME]. Target reading level: a sincere student who missed the class and must learn it from these notes alone.

YOUR TASK:
1. Write the full chapter as a printable handout: clear theory, every key formula with a one-line 'why', and short derivations of the main results.
2. Include 6-10 graded worked examples (easy to hard), each with the full method, the final boxed answer, and a 'why this works' remark.
3. Add a 'Common Traps' box (5 items) and a 'Speed Tricks / shortcuts' box where legitimate.
4. Provide a one-page formula sheet at the end and a 6-line chapter recap.
5. Insert clearly labelled placeholders like [DIAGRAM: right triangle with sides a,b,c] wherever a figure helps, so I can sketch it in.

INPUT: Here is the exact syllabus scope to cover (sub-topics, depth, anything to exclude): [PASTE SCOPE]. If I attach my textbook pages, follow their notation and sequence.

HOW TO WORK IT OUT: Derive results properly and VERIFY every worked example by a second independent method (substitute back, special case, or alternate route). Never invent formulas, constants, or values; if something is outside standard syllabus, mark it 'enrichment'. Keep all mathematics fully legible in plain ASCII (^ for powers, sqrt(), a/b for fractions, <= and >= for inequalities). Re-check each final answer before printing it.

It must also print cleanly to PDF on A4 (File > Print > Save as PDF). Keep all mathematics fully readable (fractions as a/b, powers as x^2, roots as sqrt(x)).

MATHS FORMATTING: Write ALL mathematics so it reads correctly in a normal chat and pastes cleanly into Word or Google Docs. Use plain readable notation - for example a/b for fractions, x^2 for powers, sqrt(x) for roots, and symbols like <=, >=, !=, +-, pi, theta, integral and sum. Do NOT output raw LaTeX or code such as \frac{}{}, \sqrt{}, x^{2}, $...$ or \( ... \) - these appear as broken symbols to a teacher in a free chat.
